elements.id-string-6: We consider backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and reflected BSDEs in the generality that should in principle allow for a unified study of certain discrete-time and continuous-time control problems.
elements.id-string-7: We provide well-posedness results for the BSDEs and reflected BSDEs with optional obstacle process in case of appropriately weighted $\L^2$-data.
elements.id-string-8: We compare our well-posedness results with the current literature and point out that our well-posedness result for the BSDE is sharp within the framework presented here.
elements.id-string-9: Finally, we provide sufficient conditions for a comparison principle.\vspace{5mm}{\bf Key words:}  BSDEs, reflections, general filtrations\vspace{5mm}
elements.id-string-11: Our main motivation for this work is developing backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) and reflected BSDEs in the generality that will allow an analysis of certain discrete- and continuous-time stochastic control problems in a unified manner.
elements.id-string-12: To achieve this goal, the type of systems we study in this work are, informally for now, reflected BSDEs of the form

u)(\d s,\d x) - \int_t^T \d N_s + \int_t^T \d K_s,

elements.id-string-16: Here, $T$ is a stopping time, the process $\xi$ is the obstacle, $f$ is the generator with stochastic Lipschitz coefficient $\alpha$, $X$ is the driving martingale, $\mu$ the driving random measure, and $C$ is a non-decreasing, predictable process that dominates the predictable quadratic variation $\langle X \rangle$ of $X$ and the predictable compensator $\nu$ of $\mu$.
elements.id-string-17: Note that the above system reduces to a BSDE in case $\xi = -\infty$ on $[0,T)$.
elements.id-string-18: We are then seeking to find a class of processes within which there exists a unique collection $(Y,Z,U,N,K)$ of adapted processes that solve the above system.
elements.id-string-19: In this work, we prove well-posedness of these BSDEs and reflected BSDEs under appropriately integrable $\L^2$-data $(\xi,f)$ in case the product $\alpha^2\Delta C$ is sufficiently small.
elements.id-string-20: Although not yet strictly referred to as BSDEs, the first appearance of these types of objects in case the generator $f$ is linear was in the works of \citeauthor*{bismut1973analyse} \cite{bismut1973analyse,bismut1973conjugate}, and even earlier by \citeauthor*{davis1973dynamic} \cite{davis1973dynamic}.
elements.id-string-21: In the former, BSDEs were introduced as adjoint equations that originated from an application of the Pontryagin stochastic maximum principle, and in the latter, they were used to study stochastic control problems with drift control.
elements.id-string-22: What has been recognised already in \cite{davis1973dynamic} is that value process of certain stochastic control problems can be recasted as the $Y$-component of a BSDE, which through comparison principles allows one to deduce characterisations of optimal control responses to stochastic systems.
elements.id-string-23: The first systematic study of BSDEs in the non-linear setting with Lipschitz generator was carried out by \citeauthor{pardoux1990adapted} \cite{pardoux1990adapted}, and the same authors later connected BSDEs to quasi-linear PDEs through Feynman--Kac--type formulas in \cite{pardoux1992backward}.
elements.id-string-24: The seminal survey article by \citeauthor*{el1997backward} \cite{el1997backward} collected properties of BSDEs and showed how they may be applied to solve problems in mathematical finance.
elements.id-string-25: Reflected BSDEs were introduced later by \citeauthor*{el1997reflected} \cite{el1997reflected} directly in a Lipschitz setting, where the immediate connection to optimal stopping problems and obstacle problems for parabolic PDEs was drawn.
elements.id-string-26: Concomitantly to these early contributions, reflected BSDEs have also been applied to hedging problems of American options by \citeauthor*{el1997non} \cite{el1997non}, and \citeauthor*{el1997reflected2} \cite{el1997reflected2}, and to an optimal control problem with consumption by \citeauthor*{el1998optimization} \cite{el1998optimization}, see also \citeauthor*{bally2002reflected} \cite{bally2002reflected}.
elements.id-string-27: With time, BSDEs and reflected BSDEs were applied in many areas.
elements.id-string-28: In finance, as mentioned above, for pricing of financial derivatives, see \citeauthor*{el1997backward} \cite{el1997backward} and \cite{el1997non,el1997reflected2}, or for utility maximisation problems in \citeauthor*{hu2005utility} \cite{hu2005utility}.
elements.id-string-29: One can also use BSDEs to construct recursive utilities \emph{\`a la} \citeauthor*{duffie1992asset} \cite{duffie1992asset,duffie1992stochastic}.
elements.id-string-30: There have been works on applications to zero-sum games by \citeauthor*{hamadene1995zero} \cite{hamadene1995zero} and to Dynkin games by \citeauthor*{cvitanic1996backward} \cite{cvitanic1996backward}.
elements.id-string-31: Recently, based on some new backward propagation of chaos techniques appearing in \citeauthor*{lauriere2019backward} \cite{lauriere2019backward}, BSDEs have also been applied to mean-field games by \citeauthor*{possamai2021non} \cite{possamai2021non} to deduce convergence rates of the $N$-player game to its mean-field counterpart.
elements.id-string-32: Ever since the seminal works \cite{pardoux1990adapted} and \cite{el1997reflected}, the theory of BSDEs and reflected BSDEs has expanded rapidly, and there have been various forms of generalisation of well-posedness results for these systems.
elements.id-string-33: \citeauthor*{kobylanski1997resultats} \cite{kobylanski1997resultats} and \citeauthor*{tevzadze2008solvability} \cite{tevzadze2008solvability} studied well-posedness of BSDEs with generators that are quadratic in the $z$-variable, see also the work of \citeauthor*{jackson2022characterization} \cite{jackson2022characterization} and the references therein, and \citeauthor*{kazi2015quadratic1} \cite{kazi2015quadratic1,kazi2016quadratic} as well as \citeauthor*{karoui2016quadratic} \cite{karoui2016quadratic}, \citeauthor*{jeanblanc2012robust} \cite{jeanblanc2012robust}, or \citeauthor*{matoussi2019exponential} \cite{matoussi2019exponential} for BSDEs with jumps in the quadratic case.

elements.id-string-35: Another possible direction of generalisation is to consider BSDEs and reflected BSDEs on random time horizon.

elements.id-string-59: Our main contributions are two well-posedness results, one for BSDEs and one for reflected BSDEs.
elements.id-string-60: In the BSDE case, the well-posedness result we present turns out to be sharp within the framework we lay out and cannot be improved with our methods, due to counterexamples to existence and uniqueness in \citeauthor*{confortola2014backward} \cite{confortola2014backward}.

elements.id-string-62: The method of proof we use is based on a fixed-point argument and \emph{a priori} estimates that we establish by techniques that are inspired by \cite{elkaroui1997general}, although we do not use exponential weights like in \cite{elkaroui1997general,papapantoleon2018existence}, but stochastic exponential weights like in \cite{bandini2015existence,cohen2012existence}.
elements.id-string-63: With the techniques in \cite{elkaroui1997general}, we can exploit the $\L^2$-structure of our problem, allowing us to circumvent a reliance on It\^o's formula.
elements.id-string-64: In the reflected BSDE case, we will also use a fixed-point argument and \emph{a priori} estimates.

elements.id-string-67: We thus approach this problem differently, and apply it in combination with the methods in \cite{elkaroui1997general} and \cite{grigorova2020optimal} to deduce the desired \emph{a priori} estimates.
elements.id-string-68: To the best of our knowledge, the well-posedness result we will present in the reflected BSDE case is the first of its kind in case the integrator $C$ is allowed to jump.

elements.id-string-71: BSDEs and reflected BSDEs are intimately connected to control problems with drift control only since there the dynamic programming equation is semi-linear (thus quasi-linear).
elements.id-string-72: However, for stochastic control problems with drift and volatility control, the dynamic programming equation is fully non-linear and can thus not be analysed by classical BSDEs.
elements.id-string-73: This fact was the starting point for the new notion of second-order BSDEs (2BSDEs) introduced by \citeauthor*{cheridito2007second} \cite{cheridito2007second} and \citeauthor*{soner2011quasi} \cite{soner2011quasi,soner2012wellposedness}.
elements.id-string-74: Here, the $Y$-component of these 2BSDEs corresponds to the classical value process of a control problem with drift and volatility control.

elements.id-string-81: The remainder of this paper is structured as follows: In \Cref{sec::preliminaries}, we recall preliminaries on (vector) stochastic integration and orthogonal decompositions of martingales.
elements.id-string-82: We also fix the data and formulate the BSDE and reflected BSDE.
elements.id-string-83: In \Cref{sec::main_results}, we formulate our main results, separately, for the reflected BSDE first, and then for the BSDE.
elements.id-string-84: We also compare our assumptions with the current literature.
elements.id-string-85: In \Cref{sec::optimal_stopping}, we revisit the Snell envelope and optimal stopping theory, with which we solve the reflected BSDE in case of a generator not depending on the solution.
elements.id-string-86: In \Cref{sec::a_priori}, we establish the \emph{a priori} estimates, which we will use in the contraction argument, separately in the reflected BSDE case first, and then in the BSDE case.
elements.id-string-87: We then establish the two well-posedness results in \Cref{sec::existence_rbsde}.
elements.id-string-88: Finally, we prove a comparison result for our BSDE in \Cref{sec::comparison}.
elements.id-string-89: The appendices contain proofs of technical results and some auxiliary results we make use of throughout this work.

elements.id-string-111: Preliminaries and formulation of the reflected BSDE
elements.id-string-112: This section will lay the foundations for the analysis that follows.
elements.id-string-113: We recall the construction and some properties of the vector stochastic integral and compensated stochastic integral with respect to an integer-valued random measure.

elements.id-string-116: We fix once and for all a probability space $(\Omega,\cF,\P)$ and a right-continuous filtration $\G = (\cG_t)_{t \in [0,\infty)}$.
elements.id-string-117: We denote by $\cG_\infty \coloneqq \cG_{\infty-}$ the $\sigma$-algebra on $\Omega$ generated by the sets in $\cup_{t \in [0,\infty)} \cG_t$.

elements.id-string-119: The universal completion of a $\sigma$-algebra $\cA$ is the $\sigma$-algebra $\cA^U \coloneqq \cap_{\P^\prime\in\Pc(\Omega,\Ac)} \cA^{\P^\prime}$, where the intersection is over the set $\Pc(\Omega,\Ac)$ of all probability measures $\P^\prime$ on $(\Omega,\cA)$.
